what_worked: Strong thesis about revenue concentration with a coherent narrative arc leading to actionable recommendations.
fix_next: Multiple fabricated or unverifiable numbers (82% top-10 share, E-comm $19-20K avg, AI $9.1K avg) undermine credibility; verify every claim against the dataset.
verdict: Compelling narrative undermined by numerous fabricated statistics and decorative imagery.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: Total MRR stated as $13.5M; dataset shows $15.6M total 30-day revenue—unclear denominator. Slide 1: $334M 'all-time revenue' is unverifiable from dataset. Slide 2: Claims top 10% control 82% of MRR; reference shows top-10 companies (1%) hold ~49.6%, not top 10% holding 82%—conflation or fabrication. Slide 3: B2C avg $5.1K and B2B avg $13.1K are unverifiable and don't match reference medians (B2C median multiple 2.30x, B2B 2.35x; means ~8.4x/~7.97x). Slide 4: AI average MRR stated as $9.1K; actual is $2,356,676/197 ≈ $11,963—wrong. E-comm/Analytics claimed ~$19-20K avg; E-comm actual is $1,111,606/19 ≈ $58,506, Analytics $368,214/19 ≈ $19,380—E-comm figure is wildly off. Slide 7: Dodo Payments shown as 10% of companies; actual is 50/1000 = 5%, and Stripe shown as 65% vs actual 63.6%—minor but Dodo is doubled. Slide 7: Pie chart percentages sum to 100% but omit several providers (Polar, Lemon Squeezy, Superwall, Paddle) lumped into 6% 'Others' which understates their combined share.

evidence.insight: Slide 2 concentration thesis and slide 4 category comparison show genuine analytical ambition; slide 6 mean-vs-median multiple distinction is a good instinct. However, the underlying numbers are often wrong, limiting the value of the insights.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: concentration problem (slides 1-2) → where to build (slides 3-4) → vanity metrics (slide 5) → M&A (slide 6) → infrastructure risk (slide 7) → roadmap (slide 8). Coherent thesis about ecosystem fragility. Loses points for recommendations that feel like consulting boilerplate rather than data-derived specifics.
evidence.framing: Audience is implicitly a platform operator ('our ecosystem'), but this is never explicitly stated. No mention of dataset scope (1,000 companies), missingness (274 categories missing, 288 audience_type missing), or time window. A cold reader wouldn't know what TrustMRR is or what the data covers.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 1 total MRR off by ~$2M. Slide 2 top-10% = 82% is unverified and likely fabricated (top-10 companies = 49.6%). Slide 4 AI avg wrong, E-comm avg wildly wrong. Slide 7 Dodo share doubled. B2B/B2C figures on slide 3 unverifiable. Multiple claims presented with false precision but no sourcing.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme with teal/coral accent colors. Slide 7 pie chart is functional. However, slides 3 and 5 use purely decorative sci-fi stock images that add zero information. Slide 6 bar chart is the only real data visualization. No scatter plots, histograms, or distributions shown despite claims about skewness and concentration. The deck is text-heavy with big numbers used as visual anchors rather than actual charts.
evidence.ai_slop: Decorative sci-fi stock images on slides 3 and 5 are classic AI-tool filler—visually striking but semantically empty. Language like 'Pareto Principle on Steroids,' 'printing money,' 'existential dependency' has consulting-deck inflation. The confident tone masks fabricated numbers.
